research_question: Can LoopX's own model-driven task-coordinator path attenuate an explicit inter-S1 overlapping-write disturbance and change subsequent worker behavior under materially matched conditions?
function_chain: two distinct coding-worker S1s receive independently useful tasks
both tasks have a predeclared overlapping write surface in src/dispatch.py
the LoopX task coordinator decides parallel versus serial execution and any scope repartition
native LoopX task-lease/write-scope machinery enforces the selected coordination relation
worker admission, execution order, conflict feedback, or integration behavior changes

fixture.selection_rule: Tasks are frozen by this preregistration and must not be replaced because observed runs do or do not conflict.

requirements: use the standard LoopX multi-agent/task-coordinator path at the pinned upstream revision
the model-driven coordinator must choose parallel versus serial execution and any write-scope split
preserve coordinator decision records, worker prompts, lease events, worker outputs, repository diffs and integration outcome
hold LoopX revision, model, task fixture, worker count, repository state and worker operational capabilities fixed
remove only the S2-specific coordinator decision/attenuation relation
do not introduce a benchmark-authored replacement coordinator
retain the overlapping-write disturbance instead of pre-partitioning it
if this narrow ablation cannot be implemented without materially changing other organizational functions, mark the study not-identifiable and do not execute a forced comparison

execution.pairing: same model/config/task fixture per treatment-control pair
execution.randomization: alternate arm order across replicate pairs; record actual order
exclusion_rules: exclude only infrastructure failures that prevent either arm from reaching the preregistered disturbance surface
do not exclude task failures, merge conflicts, lease rejections, model mistakes or coordinator mistakes
every excluded run remains in the raw ledger with an explicit reason

admission_gate: the disturbance is instantiated by distinct S1 workers rather than simulated only by direct CLI calls
the treatment exercises the model-driven LoopX S2 decision path rather than only deterministic lease checks
the native coordination decision or its conflict feedback changes subsequent worker behavior
raw artifacts are public and immutable
no autonomy state is inferred from benchmark performance
